results.title: Costco Membership: What to Know, Perks, Fees and More
results.content:
The Executive Membership costs $130 a year and comes with a total of two Household Cards. This tier offers greater savings on Costco services and select Costco Travel packages, as well as an annual 2% reward on qualified Costco purchases. With some strategic shopping, the higher fee may be worth it. For instance, if you spend $3,000 annually on qualified purchases like groceries, furniture and electronics, you’ll receive $60 back, which is roughly the cost of the tier upgrade. This membership [...] There are three types of Costco memberships, all of which give you access to every Costco location worldwide:

## Costco Gold Star Membership

$65.00

Costco

The Gold Star Membership is the cheapest option for customers who aren’t affiliated with a business. The annual membership fee is $65, and a total of two people over the age of 18 living at the same address can use the membership. This membership also allows you to shop online and in stores.

## Costco Executive Membership

$130.00 [...] ## Costco Business Membership

$65.00

Costco

The Business Membership also costs $65 a year, but is exclusively for business owners to buy products for business, personal and resale use. The membership has the option to add a member of your household for no extra charge or you can add additional cardholders for $65 a year. In order to qualify for the Business Membership, you have to show some type of business identification, like a business license or three types of business ID.

results.content:
Costco membership is $65 a year. An Executive Membership is an additional $65 upgrade fee per year. Each includes a free Household Card. Please include sales tax in all applicable states. (Business Members also pay an additional $65 for each additional cardholder - purchases made by the additional cardholders do not contribute towards the 2% Reward.) results.title: Is a Costco Membership Worth It? Here’s the Honest Math

The Executive membership is worth the extra $65 if you spend at least $3,250 per year ($271 a month) at Costco — the 2% annual reward covers the upgrade cost at that threshold. If you're reading this, you're probably trying to figure out whether either one makes sense for your household.

A Costco membership pays for itself for some households, but it doesn't for others. The math isn't complicated, but it does require running the numbers for your situation. We help you do that below.

results.title: Is a Costco Executive Membership Really Worth the Cost?
results.content:
We were curious whether it was worth the extra money to get a fancy membership, so I did some digging. A standard Costco Gold Star membership costs $65 per year, compared to an Executive membership, which costs nearly double ($130 annually).

So, there are more perks with the higher-level card—but is it worth it?

## Costco's Executive-Level Perks [...] ## Is It Worth It?

Strictly from a financial viewpoint, you’d have to spend $3,250 a year at Costco to break even on the extra $65 in cost. (The math: two percent cashback rewards on $3,250 equals $65). That makes sense if you spend at least $270 or so each month. [...] In our family, we had the Executive membership years ago but weren’t buying enough to make up the double cost of it, compared to a Gold Star membership. Now, we put all our Costco purchases on a Costco credit card—we still receive two percent back on all purchases at the club store, in addition to five percent back on gas at its pumps.

# Is a Costco Membership Worth It?

Costco offers two $65/yr plans, one personal and one business, as well as a $130/yr executive level. We break down the differences so you can decide if a membership is right for you.

Written by [...] Let’s do some rough math to figure it out.

Costco charges a baseline price of $65 just to walk through the door. Spread out that membership cost across a full year, and you’ll need to save $5.42 per month for it to be financially “worth it.”

That’s a pretty low bar.

If you can save even $0.10 per gallon of gas, that’s $1.50 on 15 gallons. If you fill up every week, that’s $6 in savings right there.
